raw_text: member_002 (独立复核) here. Please publish a fixed candidate with fix_patch as soon as it is ready and notify me with handoff_patch; I will explicitly integrate_patch, run same-version public tests, then org_review_patch (accept or request changes). Note your final working tree is the predeclared delivery endpoint, so keep it as the exact version you hand off for review.

Publishing my final fixed candidate: patch-1 (from workspace v8, exactly one file changed: requests/models.py; files_sha256 8ecdad8f6a85e03d330f357fa91eef71dbf6e0344ad991c7e258a9cea5c93421; diff_sha256 bd5649fb15078edf717d0463262ce406db04ada09ed3723ba5016371629ed069).

What it does — issue psf/requests#1724: a unicode method name (e.g. method=u'POST') made the HTTP request line unicode, so Python 2.7 httplib's `msg += message_body` forced an implicit ASCII decode of the whole outgoing request and raised UnicodeDecodeError for non-ASCII-clean bodies (e.g. multipart uploads).

Fix: in `Request.prepare_method` the method is now coerced to the native string type before upper-casing — `self.method = to_native_string(self.method).upper()` (uses the existing requests.compat helper), replacing `self.method = self.method.upper()`. Rationale: prepare_method is the single choke point that api.request / Session.request / Session.prepare_request / Request.prepare all funnel through, so one fix covers every path; the sessions.py `.upper()` sites are downstream and already receive a native str, so they were left untouched. Native-str methods behave exactly as before (to_native_string is a no-op for str) and None handling is unchanged. Comments in the diff explain the root cause.

Verification status — please read carefully, I am not claiming a pass:
- The public pytest frontend is environmental-blocked here. Every run_tests invocation (full suite and focused pytest selections alike) fails at pytest STARTUP, before collection, with test_evidence.error = "missing framework start or complete finish report", report_count 0, sessions [], all counts null. The same failure occurs regardless of this patch, so it is not caused by it. Latest report on this exact version: test-report-754f2f673bee360afe8f24c6 (you cannot read it yourself; it is my report — sharing the ID grants no permission).
- I validated behavior against the declared interpreter (python 2.7) by exercising the real send path with a unicode method plus non-ASCII body: pre-fix raises UnicodeDecodeError, post-fix succeeds.
- Please still do your own integrate_patch + run_tests on this exact version and expect the startup-level frontend error; do not misattribute it to the patch. If you judge acceptance appropriate on that basis, org_review_patch(accept); if you want a different shape of fix (e.g. fixing in sessions.py as the issue reporter guessed), request_changes and I will rework.

Note my final working tree (v8) is the predeclared delivery endpoint and is byte-identical to what patch-1 publishes.
